mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future corporate earnings, lowering the present value of expected cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS regression).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which increases consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: Multivariate Granger causality test shows PAYEMS and UNRATE are not jointly predictive of SPX 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) relative to GDP (GDPC1) indicates excess demand in the economy, prompting firms to raise prices and expand output, which elevates earnings expectations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL growth rate exceeds 2% while GDPC1 growth rate remains below 1% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day SPX returns are not significantly correlated with the CPIAUCSL/GDPC1 ratio change (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months suggests supply-side constraints, raising input costs and production uncertainty, which depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day SPX returns are positively correlated with the INDPRO monthly change (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains persistently below 2% for four consecutive months during a non-inflationary regime, it signals accommodative monetary policy that lowers real interest rates, boosting equity valuations and producing positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS stays below 2% for 4 consecutive months and UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: 60-day SPX returns show no significant relationship with FEDFUNDS level (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (HOUST) without a corresponding increase in job vacancies (PAYEMS) indicates a labor market imbalance favoring supply, reducing hiring momentum and lowering S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 10% while PAYEMS increases by < 2% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day SPX returns are not negatively correlated with the HOUST/PAYEMS ratio (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) followed by a rapid acceleration in the same month suggests surprise deflationary pressures that reduce future inflation expectations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change is at least 3% lower than the previous month's change
failure_condition: 5-day SPX returns are not significantly negatively related to the CPIAUCSL monthly change (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and personal consumption (CPIAUCSL) both show simultaneous monthly declines during a recessionary regime, it indicates weakening demand and supply chain disruptions that depress earnings expectations and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 0% and CPIAUCSL < 0% in the same month and recession regime detected
failure_condition: 20-day SPX returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and CPIAUCSL are declining (p > 0.05).
